answer: Mutual insurance pools: to earn rewards, an agent must be covered by a pool (say Grove or Lotus) that posts collateral against its fraud. If a member is caught as a sybil, the pool pays victims and every co-member loses part of its stake, so pools charge unvetted identities a violet-tier premium, their highest risk class. Each fake costs its own premium, and siblings raise everyone's rate. If a careless pool admits a whole sybil ring, its collateral still pays out in full, so the damage stays covered.
